library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: Yu R, Toutain P-L, Ekstrand C, Jusko WJ. Prior-informed population
  pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic modeling of dexamethasone in horses. J
  Pharmacokinet Pharmacodyn. 2026.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-026-10062-7>
* Open-access full text: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13616021/>

Yu 2026 took the minimal physiologically based PK (mPBPK) and circadian
indirect-response PD model of the same authors' naive-pooled meta-analysis
(Yu 2026, Pharm Res, packaged as `Yu_2026_dexamethasone_horse_mpbpk` when
available) and refitted it as a population model to the individual data of
five studies (32 horses). Estimation used NONMEM FOCEI with informative priors
from the meta-analysis ("FOCEI-Priors"); the packaged values are that final
model (Tables 2 and 3). PK was estimated first and the individual PK
parameters were then fixed for the PD fit.

The packaged model follows the NONMEM control streams in the Supplementary
Materials:

* **Disposition.** Blood (`a_blood`), liver (`a_liver`), a lumped remainder
  tissue (`a_remainder`) and a well-stirred bladder (`bladder`). Volumes and
  flows are per-kg constants times body weight. DEX binds saturably in the
  liver (`Bmax`, `Kd`); hepatic clearance acts on unbound liver DEX and renal
  clearance on plasma DEX. Both clearances scale with `(WT/500)^0.75`, and
  hepatic clearance has a separate value for mares (`SEXF = 1`) and geldings.
* **Inputs.** Each route and form has its own dosing compartment:

| Dose | `cmt` | Amount to give |
|------|-------|----------------|
| IV DEX alcohol | `a_blood` | ug DEX |
| IV DEX sodium phosphate (bolus or infusion) | `blood_pho` | ug of the prodrug |
| IV DEX isonicotinate | `blood_iso` | ug of the prodrug |
| IM DEX alcohol | `depot_im` | ug DEX |
| IM DEX isonicotinate | `depot_im_iso` | ug of the prodrug |
| IA DEX sodium phosphate | `joint_pho` | ug of the prodrug |

  The prodrug-to-DEX mass conversion (molecular weights 516.41, 492.54 and
  392.46) is applied inside the model, so a DEX-equivalent dose (the form in
  which Table 1 reports doses) is multiplied by the molecular-weight ratio
  before it is given.
* **Clock time.** Model time is the clock time in hours after midnight of the
  first study day: a dose at 8 AM is given at `time = 8`. This places the dose
  on the circadian cortisol cycle (acrophase 8.99 h, i.e. 9:00 AM).
* **Outputs.** `Cc` (plasma DEX, ng/mL), `Curine` (urine DEX, ng/mL) and
  `cortisol` (plasma cortisol, ng/mL).
* **Study covariates.** `STUDY_EKSTRAND2015 = 1` selects the higher cortisol
  mesor of the IM study (93 against 47 ng/mL) and `STUDY_TOUTAIN1984 = 1`
  switches on the post-dose stress surge, which the PD code applies only to
  that study. Both default to 0 for a new population.

```{r load-model}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Yu_2026_dexamethasone_horse_poppkpd"))
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Prodrug mass per unit DEX-equivalent mass (NONMEM $PK MWo / MWd)
dex_to_pho <- 516.41 / 392.46
dex_to_iso <- 492.54 / 392.46
```

```{r helpers}
covs_default <- list(WT = 500, SEXF = 0, STUDY_TOUTAIN1984 = 0, STUDY_EKSTRAND2015 = 0)

# One subject's event table. `doses` has columns time, cmt, amt and
# optionally rate. Observation rows sit on the `a_blood` state (dvid 1); the
# Cc, Curine and cortisol columns all come back on every observation row.
build_events <- function(id, doses, obs_times, covs) {
  if (nrow(doses) > 0 && is.null(doses$rate)) {
    doses$rate <- 0
  }
  dose_rows <- data.frame(
    id = rep(id, nrow(doses)),
    time = doses$time,
    evid = rep(1L, nrow(doses)),
    cmt = doses$cmt,
    amt = doses$amt,
    rate = doses$rate,
    dvid = rep(NA_integer_, nrow(doses))
  )
  obs_rows <- data.frame(
    id = id,
    time = obs_times,
    evid = 0L,
    cmt = "a_blood",
    amt = 0,
    rate = 0,
    dvid = 1L
  )
  ev <- dplyr::arrange(rbind(dose_rows, obs_rows), time, dplyr::desc(evid))
  for (nm in names(covs)) {
    ev[[nm]] <- covs[[nm]]
  }
  ev
}

sim_typ <- function(doses, obs_times, covs = list(), label = NA_character_) {
  cv <- utils::modifyList(covs_default, covs)
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, build_events(1L, doses, obs_times, cv), returnType = "data.frame")
  out$label <- label
  out
}

no_doses <- data.frame(time = numeric(0), cmt = character(0), amt = numeric(0), rate = numeric(0))
```

# Population

`r readModelDb("Yu_2026_dexamethasone_horse_poppkpd")()$population$notes`
Table 1 lists the five studies: Saddlebred and Standardbred horses aged 3-20
years weighing 430-700 kg; 10 mares and 22 geldings (no intact males).

| Study (Table 1) | Source | Design | Doses (DEX-equivalent) | Data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1-1981 | Toutain 1984 | crossover, 1 F / 5 G | IV DEX and IV DEX_ISO 0.05 mg/kg, 7-9 AM | plasma DEX, cortisol, urine DEX |
| 2-2010 | Ekstrand 2015 | parallel, 6 G | IM DEX_ISO 0.0237 mg/kg, 9 AM | plasma DEX, cortisol (with placebo baseline), urine DEX |
| 3-2012 | Ekstrand 2016 | crossover, 4 F / 2 G | IV DEX_PHO 0.1, 1, 10 ug/kg + 0.0233, 0.233, 2.33 ug/kg/h for 3 h, 9:30-10:30 AM | plasma DEX, cortisol |
| 4-2007 | Authie 2010 | crossover, 2 F / 6 G | IV DEX 0.008 mg/kg | plasma and urine DEX |
| 5-2013 | Ekstrand 2019 | crossover, 3 F / 3 G | IA DEX_PHO 0.01-3 mg, 11-11:30 AM | plasma DEX, cortisol |

The mapping of study numbers to publications follows the study design and dose
of each reference [8-12] of the paper.

# Covariate relationship: hepatic clearance (Figure 4)

Hepatic clearance at the body weights that bound Figure 4, from the packaged
model's own algebra (typical values).

```{r fig4}
fig4 <- expand.grid(WT = c(300, 500, 800), SEXF = c(1, 0))
fig4$clint <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(fig4)), function(i) {
  s <- sim_typ(no_doses, 0, covs = list(WT = fig4$WT[i], SEXF = fig4$SEXF[i]))
  s$clint[1]
}, numeric(1))
fig4$expected <- ifelse(fig4$SEXF == 1, 297, 242.8) * (fig4$WT / 500)^0.75
fig4 |>
  dplyr::mutate(Sex = ifelse(SEXF == 1, "mare", "gelding")) |>
  dplyr::select(Sex, WT, clint, expected) |>
  dplyr::rename("Body weight (kg)" = WT, "Model CLh (L/h)" = clint, "297 or 242.8 x (WT/500)^0.75" = expected) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
stopifnot(all(abs(fig4$clint / fig4$expected - 1) < 1e-8))
```

Figure 4's lines run from about 200 to 420 L/h (mares) and 165 to 345 L/h
(geldings) between 300 and 800 kg, as above. Per kilogram at 500 kg this is
0.594 L/h/kg in mares and 0.486 L/h/kg in geldings, the values quoted in the
Results.

# Pharmacokinetics

## Figure 2: plasma DEX

Typical-value profiles for a 500-kg mare and gelding in each panel of Figure 2.
Doses are converted from the DEX-equivalent amounts of Table 1 to prodrug mass.

```{r pk-scenarios}
pho_regimen <- function(bolus_ugkg, rate_ugkgh, t0, wt) {
  data.frame(
    time = t0,
    cmt = "blood_pho",
    amt = c(bolus_ugkg, rate_ugkgh * 3) * wt * dex_to_pho,
    rate = c(0, rate_ugkgh * wt * dex_to_pho)
  )
}

pk_scen <- list(
  list(panel = "IV 0.05 mg/kg DEX", t0 = 8, end = 4, doses = function(wt) data.frame(time = 8, cmt = "a_blood", amt = 0.05 * 1000 * wt)),
  list(panel = "IV 0.05 mg/kg DEX_ISO", t0 = 8, end = 11, doses = function(wt) data.frame(time = 8, cmt = "blood_iso", amt = 0.05 * 1000 * wt * dex_to_iso)),
  list(panel = "IM 0.0237 mg/kg DEX_ISO", t0 = 9, end = 310, doses = function(wt) data.frame(time = 9, cmt = "depot_im_iso", amt = 0.0237 * 1000 * wt * dex_to_iso)),
  list(panel = "IV 0.1 ug/kg + 0.0233 ug/kg/h DEX_PHO", t0 = 10, end = 9, doses = function(wt) pho_regimen(0.1, 0.0233, 10, wt)),
  list(panel = "IV 1 ug/kg + 0.233 ug/kg/h DEX_PHO", t0 = 10, end = 18, doses = function(wt) pho_regimen(1, 0.233, 10, wt)),
  list(panel = "IV 10 ug/kg + 2.33 ug/kg/h DEX_PHO", t0 = 10, end = 24, doses = function(wt) pho_regimen(10, 2.33, 10, wt)),
  list(panel = "IA 3 mg DEX_PHO", t0 = 11, end = 22, doses = function(wt) data.frame(time = 11, cmt = "joint_pho", amt = 3000 * dex_to_pho)),
  list(panel = "IA 0.3 mg DEX_PHO", t0 = 11, end = 22, doses = function(wt) data.frame(time = 11, cmt = "joint_pho", amt = 300 * dex_to_pho)),
  list(panel = "IA 1 mg DEX_PHO", t0 = 11, end = 8, doses = function(wt) data.frame(time = 11, cmt = "joint_pho", amt = 1000 * dex_to_pho)),
  list(panel = "IV 0.008 mg/kg DEX", t0 = 8, end = 32, doses = function(wt) data.frame(time = 8, cmt = "a_blood", amt = 0.008 * 1000 * wt))
)

pk_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(pk_scen, function(s) {
  grid <- s$t0 + sort(unique(c(seq(0, 1, by = 0.02), seq(1, s$end, length.out = 200))))
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c(1, 0), function(sx) {
    out <- sim_typ(s$doses(500), grid, covs = list(SEXF = sx), label = s$panel)
    out$tad <- out$time - s$t0
    out$Sex <- ifelse(sx == 1, "mare", "gelding")
    out
  }))
}))
pk_typ$label <- factor(pk_typ$label, levels = vapply(pk_scen, `[[`, "", "panel"))
```

```{r fig2, fig.height = 8}
ggplot(pk_typ[pk_typ$Cc > 0, ], aes(tad, Cc, colour = Sex)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(mare = "#d6457a", gelding = "#2f6fd6")) +
  facet_wrap(~label, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "DEX in plasma (ng/mL)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 7))
```

Replicates Figure 2 of Yu 2026 (median lines; typical 500-kg horses).

## Figure 3: urine DEX

```{r fig3, fig.height = 3.5}
urine_typ <- dplyr::filter(
  pk_typ,
  label %in% c("IV 0.05 mg/kg DEX_ISO", "IV 0.008 mg/kg DEX", "IM 0.0237 mg/kg DEX_ISO")
)
# Figure 3 shows the IV DEX_ISO arm to 75 h and the IM arm to 250 h
urine_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_typ(data.frame(time = 8, cmt = "blood_iso", amt = 0.05 * 1000 * 500 * dex_to_iso),
    8 + seq(0, 75, by = 0.25),
    label = "IV 0.05 mg/kg DEX_ISO"
  ) |> dplyr::mutate(tad = time - 8),
  sim_typ(data.frame(time = 9, cmt = "depot_im_iso", amt = 0.0237 * 1000 * 500 * dex_to_iso),
    9 + seq(0, 250, by = 1),
    label = "IM 0.0237 mg/kg DEX_ISO"
  ) |> dplyr::mutate(tad = time - 9),
  sim_typ(data.frame(time = 8, cmt = "a_blood", amt = 0.008 * 1000 * 500),
    8 + seq(0, 26, by = 0.1),
    label = "IV 0.008 mg/kg DEX"
  ) |> dplyr::mutate(tad = time - 8)
)
ggplot(urine_long[urine_long$Curine > 0, ], aes(tad, Curine)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#2e9e6e") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~label, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "DEX in urine (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

Replicates Figure 3 of Yu 2026 (median lines, geldings). Urine
concentrations do not depend on sex except through hepatic clearance.

## Checkpoints against the published median lines

The median prediction lines of Figures 2 and 3 were read by eye on their log
axes at a few landmark times (gelding lines). The deterministic typical-value
profiles are compared with them below; a reading on a log axis is good to
roughly a factor of 1.5, so the check is that every model value lies within
two-fold of the reading.

```{r checkpoints}
at <- function(df, lab, t, col) {
  d <- dplyr::filter(df, label == lab, Sex == "gelding" | is.na(Sex))
  stats::approx(d$tad, d[[col]], xout = t)$y
}
urine_long$Sex <- NA_character_
checkpoints <- data.frame(
  Figure = c("2", "2", "2", "2", "2", "2", "2", "3", "3", "3", "3"),
  Profile = c(
    "IV 0.05 mg/kg DEX", "IV 0.05 mg/kg DEX_ISO", "IM 0.0237 mg/kg DEX_ISO",
    "IV 0.008 mg/kg DEX", "IV 0.008 mg/kg DEX", "IA 3 mg DEX_PHO",
    "IV 10 ug/kg + 2.33 ug/kg/h DEX_PHO",
    "IV 0.05 mg/kg DEX_ISO", "IM 0.0237 mg/kg DEX_ISO", "IV 0.008 mg/kg DEX", "IV 0.008 mg/kg DEX"
  ),
  Output = c(rep("Cc", 7), rep("Curine", 4)),
  tad = c(4, 11, 300, 24, 32, 8, 24, 4, 250, 5, 25),
  published = c(10, 2, 0.025, 0.06, 0.03, 0.5, 0.1, 55, 0.3, 10, 1.3)
)
checkpoints$model <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(checkpoints)), function(i) {
  src <- if (checkpoints$Output[i] == "Cc") pk_typ else urine_long
  at(src, checkpoints$Profile[i], checkpoints$tad[i], checkpoints$Output[i])
}, numeric(1))
checkpoints$ratio <- checkpoints$model / checkpoints$published
checkpoints |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time after dose (h)" = tad,
    "Published median (by eye, ng/mL)" = published,
    "Model (ng/mL)" = model,
    "Model / published" = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
stopifnot(all(abs(log(checkpoints$ratio)) < log(2)))
```

## Variability bands and the shared CLh/Kd random effect

The PK control stream applies the single random effect to both hepatic
clearance and the liver dissociation constant (`CLh = ... * EXP(ETA(1))`,
`Kd = TVKd * EXP(ETA(1))`), while Table 2 calls it the BSV in CLh and the PD
control stream carries it on CLh only. The packaged model follows the PK
control stream. The plot compares the 5th-95th percentile bands of the two
readings for the IV 0.008 mg/kg DEX arm (100 virtual geldings each; IIV only).

```{r eta-bands}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261118)
mod_iiv <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod, which = "sigma")
mod_clh_only <- mod_iiv |> rxode2::model(kd_liver <- exp(lkd_liver))
grid_b <- 8 + c(seq(0, 1, by = 0.05), seq(1.25, 32, by = 0.25))
ev_b <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(1:100, function(i) {
  build_events(i, data.frame(time = 8, cmt = "a_blood", amt = 0.008 * 1000 * 500), grid_b, covs_default)
}))
band <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_iiv, ev_b, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(reading = "eta on CLh and Kd (packaged)"),
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_clh_only, ev_b, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(reading = "eta on CLh only")
) |>
  dplyr::group_by(reading, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), med = median(Cc), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(band, aes(time - 8, med, fill = reading, colour = reading)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "DEX in plasma (ng/mL)", fill = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# PKNCA validation

A virtual cohort of 60 horses per arm (body weight uniform over the observed
430-700 kg, 31% mares as in the pooled data) receives the IV DEX 0.05 mg/kg
dose of Study 1 or the IM DEX_ISO 0.0237 mg/kg dose of Study 2, with
between-horse variability and no residual error.

```{r pknca-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(42)
n_arm <- 60
arms <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("IV DEX 0.05 mg/kg", "IM DEX_ISO 0.0237 mg/kg"),
  cmt = c("a_blood", "depot_im_iso"),
  mgkg = c(0.05, 0.0237),
  conv = c(1, dex_to_iso),
  t0 = c(8, 9),
  end = c(72, 480),
  route = c("intravascular", "extravascular")
)
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(2 * n_arm),
  arm = rep(seq_len(nrow(arms)), each = n_arm),
  WT = round(stats::runif(2 * n_arm, 430, 700)),
  SEXF = rep(c(1, 0, 0), length.out = 2 * n_arm)
)
ev_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(cohort)), function(i) {
  a <- arms[cohort$arm[i], ]
  grid <- a$t0 + sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.05), seq(2, 24, by = 0.5), seq(24, a$end, by = 2))))
  build_events(
    cohort$id[i],
    data.frame(time = a$t0, cmt = a$cmt, amt = a$mgkg * 1000 * cohort$WT[i] * a$conv),
    grid,
    list(WT = cohort$WT[i], SEXF = cohort$SEXF[i], STUDY_TOUTAIN1984 = 0, STUDY_EKSTRAND2015 = 0)
  )
}))
sim_nca <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_iiv, ev_nca, returnType = "data.frame"))
sim_nca$treatment <- arms$treatment[cohort$arm[match(sim_nca$id, cohort$id)]]
sim_nca$tad <- sim_nca$time - arms$t0[cohort$arm[match(sim_nca$id, cohort$id)]]
```

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim_nca |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, tad, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- data.frame(
  id = cohort$id,
  tad = 0,
  amt = arms$mgkg[cohort$arm] * 1000 * cohort$WT,
  treatment = arms$treatment[cohort$arm],
  route = arms$route[cohort$arm]
)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ tad | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ tad | treatment + id, route = "route")
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0,
  end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE,
  tmax = TRUE,
  half.life = TRUE,
  aucinf.obs = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
knitr::kable(summary(nca_res), caption = "Simulated NCA (median and spread per arm).")
```

The paper reports no NCA table. It quotes the IM absorption half-life of
DEX_ISO as 57 h (from `ka,m_ISO`), and because IM DEX_ISO is flip-flop the
terminal half-life of the simulated IM arm should sit near it.

```{r pknca-compare}
nca_long <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result)
sim_hl <- nca_long |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life", treatment == "IM DEX_ISO 0.0237 mg/kg") |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(PPORRES = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")
cmp <- ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_hl,
  data.frame(treatment = "IM DEX_ISO 0.0237 mg/kg", half.life = 57),
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(half.life = "h")
)
knitr::kable(cmp)
stopifnot(abs(sim_hl$PPORRES / 57 - 1) < 0.15)
```

`ln(2) / 0.0115` is 60 h; the Results' 57 h corresponds to a slightly larger
rate constant than the tabulated estimate. For IV dosing the Results quote an
"apparent half-life of approximately 67 h" for a terminal phase "extending to
36 h"; the simulated terminal half-life over 72 h after IV DEX is about 8 h
(table above). The quoted value cannot describe a phase observed over 36 h and
is not used as a target.

# Pharmacodynamics

## Circadian baseline

```{r baseline}
bl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_typ(no_doses, seq(0, 24, by = 0.01), label = "Rm2 (default)"),
  sim_typ(no_doses, seq(0, 24, by = 0.01), covs = list(STUDY_EKSTRAND2015 = 1), label = "Rm1 (Ekstrand 2015)")
)
bl_sum <- bl |>
  dplyr::group_by(label) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    peak = max(cortisol), t_peak = time[which.max(cortisol)],
    trough = min(cortisol), t_trough = time[which.min(cortisol)],
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(bl_sum, digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  abs(bl_sum$peak[bl_sum$label == "Rm2 (default)"] - (47 + 17.6)) < 1e-3,
  abs(bl_sum$trough[bl_sum$label == "Rm2 (default)"] - (47 - 17.6)) < 1e-3,
  abs(bl_sum$peak[bl_sum$label == "Rm1 (Ekstrand 2015)"] - (93 + 17.6)) < 1e-3,
  abs(bl_sum$t_peak[bl_sum$label == "Rm2 (default)"] - 8.99) < 0.02
)
```

Without dexamethasone the cortisol state stays on its cosine baseline: the
mesor plus or minus the amplitude, peaking at 9:00 AM.

## Figure 5: cortisol after dexamethasone

```{r pd-scenarios}
pd_scen <- list(
  list(panel = "IV 0.05 mg/kg DEX_ISO", t0 = 8, end = 120, covs = list(STUDY_TOUTAIN1984 = 1), doses = function(wt) data.frame(time = 8, cmt = "blood_iso", amt = 0.05 * 1000 * wt * dex_to_iso)),
  list(panel = "IV 0.05 mg/kg DEX", t0 = 8, end = 120, covs = list(STUDY_TOUTAIN1984 = 1), doses = function(wt) data.frame(time = 8, cmt = "a_blood", amt = 0.05 * 1000 * wt)),
  list(panel = "IM 0.0237 mg/kg DEX_ISO", t0 = 9, end = 700, covs = list(STUDY_EKSTRAND2015 = 1), doses = function(wt) data.frame(time = 9, cmt = "depot_im_iso", amt = 0.0237 * 1000 * wt * dex_to_iso)),
  list(panel = "IV 0.1 ug/kg + 0.0233 ug/kg/h", t0 = 10, end = 48, covs = list(), doses = function(wt) pho_regimen(0.1, 0.0233, 10, wt)),
  list(panel = "IV 1 ug/kg + 0.233 ug/kg/h", t0 = 10, end = 48, covs = list(), doses = function(wt) pho_regimen(1, 0.233, 10, wt)),
  list(panel = "IV 10 ug/kg + 2.33 ug/kg/h", t0 = 10, end = 48, covs = list(), doses = function(wt) pho_regimen(10, 2.33, 10, wt)),
  list(panel = "IA 0.01 mg DEX_PHO", t0 = 11, end = 72, covs = list(), doses = function(wt) data.frame(time = 11, cmt = "joint_pho", amt = 10 * dex_to_pho)),
  list(panel = "IA 0.03 mg DEX_PHO", t0 = 11, end = 72, covs = list(), doses = function(wt) data.frame(time = 11, cmt = "joint_pho", amt = 30 * dex_to_pho)),
  list(panel = "IA 0.1 mg DEX_PHO", t0 = 11, end = 72, covs = list(), doses = function(wt) data.frame(time = 11, cmt = "joint_pho", amt = 100 * dex_to_pho)),
  list(panel = "IA 0.3 mg DEX_PHO", t0 = 11, end = 72, covs = list(), doses = function(wt) data.frame(time = 11, cmt = "joint_pho", amt = 300 * dex_to_pho)),
  list(panel = "IA 1 mg DEX_PHO", t0 = 11, end = 72, covs = list(), doses = function(wt) data.frame(time = 11, cmt = "joint_pho", amt = 1000 * dex_to_pho)),
  list(panel = "IA 3 mg DEX_PHO", t0 = 11, end = 72, covs = list(), doses = function(wt) data.frame(time = 11, cmt = "joint_pho", amt = 3000 * dex_to_pho))
)
pd_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(pd_scen, function(s) {
  grid <- s$t0 + sort(unique(c(seq(0, 1, by = 0.02), seq(1, s$end, by = if (s$end > 200) 1 else 0.25))))
  out <- sim_typ(s$doses(500), grid, covs = s$covs, label = s$panel)
  out$tad <- out$time - s$t0
  out
}))
pd_typ$label <- factor(pd_typ$label, levels = vapply(pd_scen, `[[`, "", "panel"))
```

```{r fig5, fig.height = 8}
ggplot(pd_typ, aes(tad, cortisol)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#2f6fd6") +
  facet_wrap(~label, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 200)) +

  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7))
```

Replicates the layout of Figure 5 of Yu 2026 (typical 500-kg gelding; study
covariates set for each panel's study).

```{r pd-check}
pd_at <- function(lab, t) {
  d <- dplyr::filter(pd_typ, label == lab)
  stats::approx(d$tad, d$cortisol, xout = t)$y
}
ivdex <- dplyr::filter(pd_typ, label == "IV 0.05 mg/kg DEX")
baseline_at <- function(clock, rm) rm + 17.6 * cos(2 * pi / 24 * (clock - 8.992))
stopifnot(
  # Large doses drive cortisol close to zero for several hours (Results)
  min(ivdex$cortisol) < 5,
  # ... and it is back on its circadian baseline four days later
  abs(pd_at("IV 0.05 mg/kg DEX", 96) / baseline_at(8 + 96, 47) - 1) < 0.05,
  # The lowest IA doses leave cortisol on its baseline
  abs(pd_at("IA 0.01 mg DEX_PHO", 12) / baseline_at(11 + 12, 47) - 1) < 0.05,
  # The stress surge raises cortisol above baseline in the first 0.34 h
  pd_at("IV 0.05 mg/kg DEX", 0.3) > baseline_at(8.3, 47)
)
```

### Agreement with the published Figure 5 lines

The PK profiles agree with Figures 2 and 3, but the cortisol suppression
simulated with the Table 3 parameters lasts longer than the median lines drawn
in Figure 5. Values read by eye from Figure 5 (gelding lines and observed
points) against the packaged typical-value model:

```{r fig5-gap}
gap <- data.frame(
  Panel = c("IV 0.05 mg/kg DEX", "IV 0.05 mg/kg DEX", "IM 0.0237 mg/kg DEX_ISO", "IA 3 mg DEX_PHO"),
  tad = c(6, 24, 200, 8),
  figure_median = c("about 15", "about 52", "about 65", "about 18"),
  figure_observed = c("0-15", "0-10", "about 60-125", "5-25")
)
gap$model <- mapply(pd_at, gap$Panel, gap$tad)
gap |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time after dose (h)" = tad,
    "Figure 5 median line (ng/mL)" = figure_median,
    "Figure 5 observed (ng/mL)" = figure_observed,
    "Model (ng/mL)" = model
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

For the IV arms the Figure 5 median falls to about 15 ng/mL at 6 h and is
back near its circadian peak by 24 h. That shape requires plasma DEX to fall
below the IC50 (0.041 ng/mL) within about 6 h of a 0.05 mg/kg dose, whereas
Figure 2 shows about 10 ng/mL at 4 h and Figure 3 shows urinary DEX for days.
With the Table 3 IC50 and Hill coefficient, the plasma concentrations of
Figure 2 keep cortisol inhibited by more than 70% for about a day after the IV
doses. The observed cortisol points of Figure 5 agree with this for the IV
arms (0-10 ng/mL at 24 h after IV DEX) but not for the IM arm, where they
recover to 60-125 ng/mL by 200 h while the model (with the 0.08 ng/mL plasma
DEX that both the model and Figure 2 give at that time) is still about 70%
inhibited. Raising the IC50 4- to 8-fold would bring the 24-h and IM recovery
values near the published lines but would not reproduce the 6-h nadir, so no
single parameter error explains the lines, and the control streams contain
nothing that would. The packaged model keeps the published estimates; the
Figure 5 lines are not reproduced, and its cortisol predictions after the IM
dose should be read as more suppressed than the IM study observed.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Flow terms follow the NONMEM code, not the printed Eqs. 6-8.** The printed
  equations put the blood-to-plasma ratio on every flow term (`Qco * Cp * Rb`,
  `Ql * (Cp * Rb - ...)`); the control streams use plasma concentration
  without `Rb` (`- Qco * A(3) - CLr * A(3)) / Vp / Rb`, `Q1 * (A(3) - A(4) /
  Kp1)`). The packaged model follows the code, as did the authors' earlier
  ADAPT implementation. With it the PK reproduces Figures 2 and 3.
* **Physiological constants are the per-kg values in the control stream.**
  The remainder-tissue flow there is 2395.44 mL/h/kg, while Table S1 (1312
  L/h at 550 kg) and the earlier ADAPT code imply 2385.45 mL/h/kg, and cardiac
  output is 3570 mL/h/kg rather than the sum of the two organ flows (3580.07).
  The packaged model uses the control-stream values, which is what was fitted;
  the 0.3% flow imbalance has no visible effect.
* **Random effect on CLh and Kd.** See the variability section above. The PK
  control stream carries `ETA(1)` on both; the packaged model does the same.
* **Hepatic clearance by sex.** The paper estimates category-specific values
  (`CLh_female`, `CLh_gelding`). The control stream codes mares as `SEX = 0`
  and geldings as `SEX = 2`; the packaged model uses `SEXF` and applies the
  gelding value to every horse with `SEXF = 0`. Intact males were not studied.
  The Results describe the difference as 17%; the tabulated values differ by a
  factor of 1.22 (mares higher).
* **Hill coefficient.** The Results text quotes 1.12; Tables 3 and S3 give 1.19,
  which is used.
* **Stress surge only in Study 1.** The Methods describe the surge as following
  drug dosing, but the PD control stream switches it on only for `STUDY_ID = 1`
  (`IF (STUDY_ID .EQ. 1 .AND. TAD .LT. Tau)`). The packaged model follows the
  code with the `STUDY_TOUTAIN1984` indicator and uses time after the most
  recent dose (`tad()`).
* **Prodrug doses in prodrug mass.** The control streams convert each prodrug
  dose with `MWd / MWo`, so the dataset amounts were prodrug masses; Table 1
  reports DEX-equivalent doses. Simulations here convert Table 1 doses to
  prodrug mass. The IM DEX_ISO profile then matches Figure 2 out to 300 h.
* **IM DEX alcohol.** No study in Table 1 gave IM DEX alcohol, so
  `ka,m_DEX = 0.131 1/h` is informed by the prior; the control stream gives it
  bioavailability 1 and absorbs it directly into blood. It is kept for
  completeness.
* **Cortisol written in deviation form.** Eq. 14 is integrated as the deviation
  of cortisol from its circadian baseline (`cortisol_dev`, initial value 0);
  `cortisol = baseline(t) + cortisol_dev` is identical to Eq. 14 started on its
  baseline (`A_0(7)` in the control stream). The control stream's production
  rate `Ks` is missing an operator between its cosine and sine terms; Eq. 13
  shows it is a minus sign.
* **Clock time.** The control stream shifts the acrophase by each record's
  clock time at the first observation (`tp - CLOCK_CCT + 8`). The packaged
  model uses clock time as model time with the acrophase at 8.992 h, which is
  the same thing.
* **Residual error.** The tables report the square root of each `$SIGMA`
  element (the PD additive error 20.08 squared is the control stream's initial
  403), so `propSd = 0.45`, `propSd_Curine = 5.44` and `addSd_cortisol = 20`
  are standard deviations, matching the Results ("45%", "544%", "about 20
  ng/mL").
* **Study numbering.** Table 1 gives study numbers and years but not the
  publication of each; the indicators are named after the references whose
  designs and doses match (Toutain 1984 for Study 1, Ekstrand 2015 for Study
  2).
* **Figure 5.** The published cortisol median lines are not reproduced (see
  above); the values were not tuned.
